root_idea.summary: The root centers on extracting or delivering something from danger, capture, or adversity into safety.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from becoming safe or escaping, to rescuing another, and to designating what has been rescued. A related nominal use describes an object—especially a horse or animal—taken from another people and recovered.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form IV dictionary citation form.
Displayed as the normalized Form X dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To save, rescue, or liberate someone or something from danger, distress, an adversary, or another harmful condition.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive Form IV; the object may be delivered from a person or opponent, from evil, or from a perilous predicament. Quranic occurrences include both active and passive voice.

senses.definition: To seek or attempt to save, rescue, or liberate someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: Form X presents the rescue as sought or attempted; the object may be something to be recovered from an overpowering adversary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become safe, escape, or be saved and liberated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I. The verbal noun نَقْذ occurs in the benedictive expression نَقْذًا لَكَ, “safety to you.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or thing that has been saved, rescued, or liberated; especially a horse taken from another people, or an animal recovered from an enemy. The plural is نَقَائِذُ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe one rescued from distress or adversity and can designate a recovered possession or animal in the context of conflict.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coat of mail regarded as saving its wearer from the sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use explained through the protective function of armor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا لَهُ شَقَذٌ وَلَا نَقَذٌ: to possess nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the cited idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who has previously had a husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use of نَقِيذَةٌ.
A lexical animal name, with or without the definite article.
